name: google-drive
agentInstructions: Google Drive is a headless connector for working with Drive files. Reach for it to SEARCH Drive for a file the user references, then either READ its text content or IMPORT it as an attachment — or to UPLOAD a newly produced deliverable into Drive. Key handles: file id, file name. Write surface is DELIBERATELY NARROW: the only write is upload, which creates NEW files inside an app-owned 'Liaison Reports' folder under Google's drive.file scope — the app can never modify or delete any pre-existing file in the user's Drive (writes are only allowed on files the app itself created; reading is separate: the whole Drive via drive.readonly in mode full, only the picked files in mode picked). upload takes {name, mimeType} plus EXACTLY ONE byte source — sourceFileId (a kernel file id; PREFER this: the server reads the bytes and you carry nothing) or contentBase64 (only for small payloads you already hold: base64 is EMITTED as tool arguments, so a ~230 kB PDF is ~307 000 characters, often unsendable though inside the cap) — with a 5 MB decoded cap, and returns {fileId, webViewLink}; you cannot choose an arbitrary destination folder. Upload failures are NAMED — relay the right fix and never claim the file was uploaded: drive_scope_missing means the connection predates write access (tell the human to reconnect Drive; re-consent adds drive.file); drive_storage_full means the Google account's storage is full (free space; reconnecting will not help); drive_rate_limited means wait and retry; drive_permission_denied carries Google's reason verbatim — report it. Four tools (discover them via tool_search before answering): search (find files), upload (write a new file), read (get a file's TEXT content so you can parse/extract it in-context — a Google SHEET or an Excel workbook comes back as CSV rows, a Doc/Slides as plain text; use this when you need to WORK WITH a document's contents, e.g. parse a prospect spreadsheet's name+email rows), and import (materialise a file as a binary ATTACHMENT for a send tool — returns only a fileId, NO content). To turn spreadsheet rows into records (e.g. contacts), read the sheet, parse the real rows, and create each record yourself — there is no bulk importer, and the per-turn step budget means a large sheet (dozens of rows) can only be partially handled in one turn: be honest about that and propose a bounded subset rather than claiming you imported them all. NEVER fabricate file contents or rows the file does not contain. Silent-failure gotcha: when Drive is not connected the surface renders a not-connected state, not an error: report that and offer to connect, never fabricate files or contents. Drive mode: a Drive connected with drive.readonly reads the whole Drive (mode full). A Drive connected with drive.file only (mode picked, a personal Google account on an unverified client) sees ONLY the files and folders the person picked: search and read find nothing else. In picked mode, search answers with the picked files (pickedFiles, whatever the query; an empty query lists them): when the person mentions a file they picked, the file is in that list, so read it by its driveFileId instead of guessing names. When a file the person names is not among them, call kernel__drive_picker to show the card where they pick it; never tell them to share or move the file. In full mode never mention picking. An ORGANIZATION's Drive connection shares only the Shared Drives an admin chose, never anyone's My Drive: search and read see nothing else, and a file outside them is refused with outside_shared_drives (tell the person their own files are reached through their personal Drive connection; never suggest moving them). shared_drives_not_chosen means no shared drive is chosen yet: an admin calls shared_drives to list the shared drives the connecting account is a member of, then choose_shared_drives with the ones the team should see (a drive the account is not a member of cannot be chosen: add the account to it first).
description: Google Drive connector: a Knowledge federated-search source and a headless agent-tool surface (search + read + import Drive files, plus upload of NEW files into an app-owned 'Liaison Reports' folder under the drive.file scope; existing Drive files are never modified or deleted).

listing.summary: Search, read and import Google Drive files, and upload new reports.

setupGuide.summary: Google Drive connects over OAuth. It reads your existing files (read-only, `drive.readonly`) and can additionally CREATE new files — but only inside a folder the app itself creates ('Liaison Reports'), under Google's `drive.file` scope, which never grants access to modify or delete your pre-existing files. No password is stored.

steps.text: Ask a workspace admin to add Google OAuth credentials (one-time, per workspace).
Click **Connect** — you are redirected to Google's consent screen.

Approve read access to Drive (`drive.readonly`) for search/read/import, and per-file write access (`drive.file`) so the app can upload new files (e.g. generated reports) into its own 'Liaison Reports' folder. `drive.file` only covers files the app creates — never your existing Drive content.
Revoke any time by removing the connection here, or at myaccount.google.com/permissions.

shared_drives.description: List the organization's Google Drive connections and the Shared Drives each one shares with the team, plus (for an admin) every Shared Drive the connecting Google account is a member of, each marked chosen or not. An organization's Drive connection reads ONLY the chosen Shared Drives (never anyone's My Drive); with none chosen it reads nothing (needsSharedDrives: true). Use this before choose_shared_drives. Google lists only the drives the connecting account is a member of: a drive missing from the list needs that account added to it (any role).

choose_shared_drives.description: Choose the Shared Drives the organization's Google Drive connection shares with the team: REPLACES the chosen set with drives (each a Shared Drive id or exact name from shared_drives). Every member who may use the org connection then sees the files in them; nothing else is read (no My Drive). An empty list shares none. Each drive must be one the connecting account is a member of. Asks a person for approval first.

search.description: Search the connected Google Drive for files by name or content. Returns Drive file ids — pass one to read (its text) or import (an attachable file). In picked mode (a Drive that sees only the files the person picked) the result also lists every picked file in pickedFiles whatever the query, and an empty query lists them: look there before searching again with other words.

import.description: Pull a Google Drive file into Liaison as an attachable FILE. Returns ONLY a fileId (filename + mimeType + size) — it does NOT return the file's text/content, so you cannot read a document's body from an import result. Use this when you need the file as an ATTACHMENT on a send tool's "attachments" parameter (mail reply/compose, ticket reply, thread reply). IMPORT IS NOT THE DELIVERABLE: the returned fileId only attaches the file once you pass it into the send tool's "attachments" array — e.g. import the spec PDF, then mail__compose with attachments:["<the fileId import returned>"]. If you import a file and then send WITHOUT putting its fileId in "attachments", the file is NOT attached and you must NOT claim it is (the gated approval card would show no attachment). Native Google Docs/Sheets/Slides cannot be imported as files. DO NOT use import to bring documents INTO the Knowledge base: import gives you no content to put in a knowledge document (creating a knowledge doc from an import would force you to fabricate the body). To bring a Drive document — or a whole Drive FOLDER of documents — into Knowledge, use the knowledge folder-source harvest (add_folder_source), which reads each file's real content and creates the knowledge documents for you.

upload.description: Upload a NEW file to the connected Google Drive. Pass name (the exact filename to create), mimeType, and the bytes via EXACTLY ONE of two sources. PREFER sourceFileId: a kernel file id (from files_list, or from staging the file yourself — POST /api/files/upload-url, PUT the bytes, POST /api/files/confirm) — the server loads the bytes and you carry nothing. Use contentBase64 (the file bytes, base64-encoded) only for a small payload you already hold: base64 must be EMITTED as tool-call arguments, so a ~230 kB PDF is ~307 000 characters and can be impossible to send this way even though it is far inside the size cap. Passing both is an error. Decoded size is capped at 5 MB either way — larger uploads are refused with file_too_large. The file is ALWAYS created inside the app-owned 'Liaison Reports' Drive folder (created on first upload, recreated if deleted): under Google's drive.file scope the app can only touch files it created itself, so no arbitrary destination folder can be chosen and no existing Drive file can ever be modified or deleted. Returns {fileId, name, webViewLink, folderId} — quote the webViewLink to the user as the uploaded file's URL. Failures are named — NEVER claim the upload happened: drive_scope_missing (connection consented before write access — ask the human to reconnect Google Drive; re-consent adds drive.file), drive_storage_full (the account's Drive storage is full — free space, reconnecting won't help), drive_rate_limited (wait and retry), drive_permission_denied (relay Google's reason verbatim), source_not_found (no such kernel file is visible to you — stage it first).

read.description: Read a Google Drive file's TEXT content so you can work with it in-context (parse it, summarise it, extract rows/values). Unlike import (which returns only a fileId with no content), read returns the file's text in a `content` field. A Google SHEET comes back as CSV (one row per line — parse the header + data rows to extract structured values like a prospect's name + email); an Excel workbook (.xlsx) comes back as CSV too, each sheet under a "Sheet: <name>" line; a Google DOC or Slides comes back as plain text; a downloadable text/CSV/JSON file comes back as its raw text. Binary files (PDF, images, firmware) are NOT readable as text — use import for those. The content is real file data — never fabricate rows/values it does not contain. Note: this reads ONE file's content; it does not create contacts or any other records — you still propose those yourself per record.

member.description: Google Drive connection viewer: read connected Drive accounts, upload new files to the app-owned reports folder

admin.description: Google Drive connection administrator: manage Drive connections and policy

sections.title: Connection
sections.description: Read-only connector for searching and importing files from the connected Google Drive account.

blocks.disconnectBody: The Drive folders synced into Knowledge from this Drive account are deleted from Liaison, with the documents and links made from them. Cached Drive content is deleted only when your organization's last Drive connection is disconnected. Files you imported and documents you wrote stay. Your files stay in Google Drive.
